questions.prompt: Why is the rough ER called 'rough'?
questions.explanation: The rough ER looks bumpy because it is dotted with ribosomes, which are there to build proteins.
questions.misconception: The name is about appearance - the bumps are ribosomes doing protein work, not damage.

questions.prompt: What is one main job of the smooth ER?
questions.explanation: The smooth ER has no ribosomes and specializes in making lipids and processing many molecules.
questions.misconception: Building protein is the rough ER's job. The smooth ER focuses on fats and processing.

questions.prompt: How does the ER move materials around the cell?
options: By budding off small transport bubbles
questions.explanation: The ER packages materials into small membrane bubbles (vesicles) that carry them to other organelles or out of the cell.
questions.misconception: The ER doesn't dissolve or turn materials into water - it wraps them in bubbles and ships them.

questions.prompt: After the ER packages proteins, where do the transport bubbles usually head next?
options: To the Golgi apparatus for sorting and shipping
Back to the nucleus for storage
To the cell wall to be destroyed
questions.explanation: The ER sends its products to the Golgi apparatus, the cell's sorting and packaging center, which sends them where they are needed.
questions.misconception: Products don't return to the nucleus - they move forward down the production line to the Golgi.
